newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank to take stake in currency net system.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank to take stake in currency net system.

text.p: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd will soon take a stake in a multilateral currency netting system in a bid to eliminate foreign currency settlement risks, a bank spokesman said on Tuesday.
The spokesman said the bank plans to take a two percent, or one million pound, stake in the Exchange Clearing House (ECHO) and will be designated a settlement bank for yen.

ECHO, established in August 1995, is a multilateral currency netting system in which receivables are offset against payables to reduce the credit exposure to a particular counterparty and to minimise settlement risk.

Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd and Fuji Bank Ltd are already designated settlement banks of the British-based ECHO, but officials for both banks said it was not certain if they would take a stake in ECHO.
The Dai-Ichi Kangyo spokesman said having a stake in ECHO will give the bank a greater role in reducing its currency settlement risk.
Participants in the multilateral netting system can more effectively reduce their foreign currency settlement risks than through prevailing bilateral nettings.
Banks are exposed to large amounts of cross-border currency settlement risks because delivery of foreign exchange transactions is made in different time zones.
There is also a risk in foreign currencies settlements that after one bank has delivered one side of the transaction, its counterparty may go bankrupt and fail to deliver the offsetting currency.
